html:
The map's name, in its 1900 snapshot, for the eastern realm that Samori Ture carved out in the 1890s, in what are now northern Ivory Coast and western Ghana. It is the last phase of his Wassoulou Empire.

Driven from his homeland by French columns after 1891, Samori moved his army and much of his people east, leaving scorched land behind. He conquered new territory around Kong and Bondoukou, destroying Kong in 1897, and clashed with the British on the edge of the Gold Coast. Squeezed between the two powers, he was captured by the French in September 1898. The map's snapshot shows the empire just after its end.
